label: Glassflow
Colour
Colour source *Container colour is read from the tab itself, so tabs in different containers differ. Tabs with no container use the fallback below.*
Fallback colour *Used when a tab has no container, no folder, or the workspace has no colour set.*
Custom colour *Any CSS colour. Used when source or fallback is set to Custom.*
Darkness *Mixes the source toward black. 0% keeps Zen's pastel hue, 45% is a deep jewel tone.*
Second gradient colour *Used by gradients whose end is set to 'Fade to a second colour'.*
Glass

Colourless glass *On: blur only, no saturation or brightness shift, so glass never alters the hue behind it. Off: adds saturation and contrast, which looks richer but tints whatever is underneath. Turn this on if glass is introducing colour you did not pick.*
Glass intensity *Scales every sheen, rim and glow at once. 0 removes the glass look. The per-state switches decide where glass appears; this decides how strong.*
Sheen strength *The white highlight band only. Lower this if glass looks washed out rather than tinted. 0 removes the sheen but keeps rims and blur.*
Sheen direction *Which way the highlight band runs. Separate from each state's tint gradient.*
Selected tab
Style selected tabs *Independent switch. Everything below applies only to this state.*
Tint strength *How much source colour this state starts with.*
Opacity *Fades the whole tab including label and favicon.*
Gradient direction *Independent of every other state.*
Gradient end *What the gradient fades toward. Transparent shows whatever is behind. Weaker tint keeps the same hue at the End tint value. Second colour blends toward the Second gradient colour.*
End tint *Absolute strength at the far end. Only used by the weaker-tint and second-colour modes.*
Gradient spread *Where the fade finishes, across the tab. 100% is edge to edge; lower ends early and leaves a flat run.*
Glass sheen *The white highlight band.*
Glass rim *A 1px inner highlight along the top edge.*
Outer glow *A soft tinted halo. Replaces the rim shadow, so it includes the rim when both are on.*
Frosted blur *One compositor pass per tab in this state. The most expensive option here.*
Blur strength *Only used when frosted blur is on for this state.*

Tabs, shared
Tab roundness *Corner radius. Arc rebinds Zen's --border-radius-medium; this overrides it for tabs only.*
Texture *An overlay pattern on every tab state. Plain CSS gradients, so the cost is one extra background layer.*
Accent bar on the selected tab *A 3px bar down the left edge. Replaces Arc's container glow, which uses the same layer.*
Hide Arc's container glow *Arc paints a blurred bar of container colour across the left half of every container tab. Usually the extra colour you see on the left.*
Tab strip
Gradient behind the whole strip *One wash spanning the full strip rather than per tab. Also gives frosted blur something with structure to work against.*
Strip strength *How strong the wash is at its start.*
Strip direction *Independent of every other section.*
Sidebar
Enable sidebar styling *Tints the sidebar background. Arc's compact sidebar opacity still applies underneath; set that first, then use this on top.*
Sidebar tint *How much workspace colour the sidebar carries.*
Sidebar opacity *Fades the tinted layer.*
Sidebar gradient direction *Independent of every other section.*
Glass sheen on the sidebar *Independent switch.*
Glass rim on the sidebar *Independent switch.*
Frosted blur on the sidebar *A second blur pass on top of whatever Arc, Transparent Zen or DWMBlurGlass already apply. Stacking blurs rarely composes well.*
Sidebar blur strength *Only used when sidebar blur is on.*
Window buttons
Enable macOS-style traffic lights *Turn OFF Arc's own 'macOS style buttons' first.*
Position *Which end of the sidebar row the buttons sit on.*
Show colour at rest *Off: neutral grey until hovered.*
Vertical oval on hover *Only the button under the cursor stretches.*
Oval height multiplier *Multiple of the diameter. 1.3 is a soft oval.*
Show glyphs on hover *Triggered by hovering anywhere in the group, matching macOS.*
Glyph size *How much of the button the mark fills.*
Button opacity *Fades buttons at rest. Hover restores full opacity.*
Glass sheen on buttons *Independent switch.*
Glass rim on buttons *Independent switch.*
Frosted blur on buttons *Cheap here: three small elements, not one per tab.*
Close colour *Alpha below about 0.7 reads as glass. Hover stacks a second pass to deepen the hue.*
Minimise colour *Keep alpha below about 0.7.*
Maximise colour *Keep alpha below about 0.7.*
Diameter *macOS uses 12px, Arc uses 14px.*
Gap between buttons *macOS uses roughly 8px.*
Troubleshooting
Outline what Glassflow touches *Magenta on tabs, cyan on window buttons, orange on the sidebar. No outline means Glassflow is not matching that element.*
